decisions.reason: It is close to the core airport-operations offer and remained prominently marketed in both years, suggesting performance at or above aspiration and little need to redeploy resources away from it.
Its move from a simple mention to a dedicated page indicates rising internal commitment and satisfactory early results, while the firm's growth and slack support continued retention.

Although it appears to have gained traction by 2024, its fit with the firm's main safety-and-operations identity is somewhat less direct, so it is kept but with a somewhat higher risk of review if results disappoint.

Apron equipment monitoring fits the firm's integrated, data-driven airport strategy very well, and the stronger 2024 presentation implies it is meeting aspirations well enough to remain in the portfolio.
